findings.rule: density-tiers (boldness spent once per screen) + Section headers (no full-width tinted band)
findings.evidence: The NASCET header is a full-width solid blue band, the loudest surface on the page. The doc forbids this: 'No full-width tinted band'. The page uses 3 different header styles: tick bar (table, anatomy), blue band (NASCET), and a top ribbon plus icon tile (Recommendations; ribbons are reserved for KPI cards). findings.evidence: The segment table takes about 1,150px of height but its columns end at x≈965, so the right ~35% of the deck is empty. findings.recommendation: Relocation, not restyling, so this goes to redesign. At ≥1280px, put the anatomy diagram in a sticky right column beside the segment table, using the empty width. Move the NASCET picker under the diagram so the finding and its grade sit together.

reasoning: Inferred nothing: tier is deep-dive as supplied, compared against deep-dive.png (light). A clinician's eye goes first to the solid-blue NASCET band, the only saturated surface, then has to scroll back up through an 8-column table of empty inputs. The anatomy diagram, the screen's best visual summary, is three screens down. White decks on a white page give the screen almost no depth. Green carries two non-clinical meanings, including 'not saved yet'. Red is disciplined. The verdict is REDESIGN-REQUIRED because five dimensions score ≤1, and two of those caps are mechanical. Several fixes are only restyling: page surface token, header style, button demotion, green removal. Defects with no rule in the doc, not scored as findings: truncated column headers ('ინტიმა-მე…', 'ICA/C…'), clipped plaque multiselect chip and placeholders ('III ტიპის ç × ჯ…', 'ფოლაქის შე…'), and ICA rows at about twice the height of other rows. Highest-leverage fix: put the anatomy diagram beside the segment table as the one focal element, and turn the NASCET band into a standard tick header.
